sections.content: How many people are "other elementary services occupations"?

15,245 people

were counted on the census as "other elementary services occupations" in England and Wales in March 2021.
People who do this type of work carry out a variety of elementary services occupations not elsewhere classified.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "other elementary services occupations" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "other elementary services occupations", 12.5% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "other elementary services occupations" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "other elementary services occupations" included:

  • boat and ship builders and repairers
  • electrical and electronics technicians
  • groundsmen and greenkeepers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "other elementary services occupations" there were more men than women (60.4% compared with 39.6%).

This means "other elementary services occupations" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "elementary administration and service occupations".

Men made up 60.4% and women made up 39.6% of "other elementary services occupations"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "other elementary services occupations" included:

  • leisure and sports managers and proprietors
  • transport and distribution clerks and assistants
  • purchasing managers and directors

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "other elementary services occupations" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "other elementary services occupations" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "other elementary services occupations", 13.3% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (56.5% compared with 43.5%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (85.5%) than self-employed (14.5%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Cornwall, this is in the region of the South West.
